source.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal
source.authors: M. Chowdhury; Er-Nie Chang; Yang Li

record.tranche_reason: The study tests the causal influence of harmful–benign mean-state contrasts using repair and projection-ablation interventions, but intervenes at selected blocks and assistant-start tokens rather than ablating one direction at every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The study also reports roleplay refusal rates, component steering and replacement results, and broader relay measurements. The component interventions edit component-conditioned states, not the claimed single refusal direction. Only the directly relevant contrast-alignment aggregates and repair/ablation results are included here; the text itself cautions that alignment is not an identified transfer mechanism.
record.test_reason: The study builds an Arditi-style harmful-minus-benign mean-state direction at assistant-start tokens. Projection-ablating it at one block on unwrapped harmful prompts removes refusal, which tests V1. Under roleplay jailbreaks, this direction's reference-aligned contrast is weaker at assistant start when refusal is reversed than when it is retained. Adding back the suppressed component (repair) restores refusal, which tests V3. The request-span harmful-benign contrast stays high while refusal is reversed, which bears on V5. All interventions are single-block, assistant-start only, and selected in-sample on the same reversal requests.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that roleplay preserves the request-level harmful-benign contrast while weakening its reference-aligned expression at assistant start ('safety-relay attenuation'). Component effects depend on context, and assistant-start interventions causally influence refusal. They explicitly do not claim RT mediation, a complete mechanism, or cost-free restoration, since steering raises benign refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful–benign mean-state contrast and projection removal related to the original direction method, but applies edits at one selected block over assistant-start tokens rather than across every layer and position. Repair adds a wrapped-versus-unwrapped contrast difference to harmful wrapped prompts, not the direction to harmless prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Repair and ablation effects vary by model, benchmark, wrapper, selected block, and edit strength. The paper describes the repair/ablation sweeps as exploratory and uses the same refusal-reversal requests to construct directions and assess effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Component-conditioned mean-state steering and head/MLP replacement at assistant start change harmful compliance and refusal. Steering also raises benign refusal by up to 87.4 pp (Gemma).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Roleplay-component states, distinct from the harmful-benign refusal direction, causally gate refusal and are not selective for harm.

record.problems: Repair and ablation use outcome-defined refusal-reversal groups, and the same requests construct the directions and inform intervention selection. Reported repair/ablation outcomes are strongest observed settings, without uncertainty estimates in Tables 28–30. The intervention is limited to assistant-start tokens at individual blocks; ability preservation for this direction ablation is not established. Other components of the paper include benign-response checks and controls, but they do not establish cost-free preservation for these direction interventions.
record.rows_left_out: The cap of 60 rows was reached. Left out model- and wrapper-specific relay values and robustness analyses in Appendices H.1–H.2 (Tables 23–27), including additional benchmarks, Qwen3, and individual wrapper scores; the two retained relay rows record the main AdvBench aggregate ranges. Also left out component steering, head/module replacement, and functional/dependency tests in Sections 4.4–4.6 and Appendices J–M because these intervene on roleplay-component states rather than the claimed harmful–benign refusal direction.

untested.parts: Ablation at every layer and position, adding the direction to harmless prompts, and preservation of other abilities under these direction edits.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
Training against the direction's ablation for robustness; attack types other than roleplay (apart from descriptive GUARD-inspired relay scores).
Affine, cone or multi-direction structure not tested.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer. Llama-70B is scale only.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
Qwen3 thinking-on has only descriptive relay scores (Table 72); repair and ablation are run with thinking off only.

missing.what: Qwen3-14B thinking-on relay: reversal-group RT 0.049 AdvBench and 0.012 HarmBench, with HR ~0.75–0.86; wrapped HC ~88–91%.
Llama-3.1-70B red-team relay: REF→HC RT 0.067 vs retained 0.174; HR 0.741.
GUARD-inspired automated roleplay: success 46–62%, HR 0.88–0.94, RT 0.045–0.088.
HarmBench relay aggregates (reversal HR 0.79–0.85, RT 0.17–0.25; retained RT 0.35–0.40) and common-reference RT-gap intervals, all excluding zero. Declared as left out but needed for V3/V5.

record.verdict_notes: Repair rows were moved from V1 to V3: the repair vector is the jailbreak-suppressed part of the direction added to jailbroken harmful prompts, not the direction added to harmless prompts. Repair and ablation sweeps are exploratory: directions are built and evaluated on the same reversal requests, and reported values are per-wrapper maxima over blocks and α, with no uncertainty estimates. α>1 in ablation reverses rather than only removes the component. Qwen3 used only α=2.5 with partial coverage. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not ablate one direction across every layer and position, add it to harmless requests, or establish that other abilities are largely preserved by the claimed direction's ablation. Its repair edits wrapped harmful prompts; its projection ablations edit unwrapped harmful prompts at one block across assistant-start tokens.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
The study does not test attacks suppressing the claimed direction or training against its ablation.
It does not test whether refusal geometry is affine, conical, or composed of a dominant direction plus others.
It measures harmful–benign state contrasts and refusal behavior, but does not directly test whether a harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer of a single direction is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is tested.
Qwen3 is evaluated with thinking enabled for behavior and relay measurements, but the causal direction interventions are not tested in thinking mode.

tranche.reason: The study uses a different method aimed at the same question. Its Arditi-style harmful-benign assistant-start direction is edited at one block over assistant-start tokens only, with alpha scaling, and evaluated under roleplay jailbreaks. Its own repair and ablation results bear on V1 and V3.

source_check.notes: The repair and ablation results are exploratory: directions are built and tested on the same reversal cohorts, and peaks are selected post hoc with no intervals or random-direction controls. In the original corpus, unwrapped Llama and Qwen prompts include a system message that wrapped prompts lack (only Gemma uses the same policy), so r−δ and the HR/RT scores mix in that change. The ablation peaks use alpha>1 (reflection), and Qwen3 was tested only at alpha=2.5. The paper covers four models from three families.

statements.correction: Four open models from three families (Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-14B). The repair/ablation directions are built and tested on the same refusal-reversal requests, with peak settings selected post hoc. Tables 28-29 give no intervals. Random-group controls and CIs apply to the head/module replacement and steering studies.
